# Vendored CA certificate bundle

This directory carries the **Mozilla CA certificate store**, in PEM form, as
published by the curl project. It is the trust anchor set the vendored Mbed TLS
(`third_party/mbedtls/`) verifies a server certificate against when the vendored
libcurl (`third_party/curl/`) opens an `https://` connection.

**It is data, not source.** Nothing compiles it; `runtime/CMakeLists.txt`'s
`DN2CPP_USE_CURL` arm turns `cacert.pem` into a C++ byte array at build time (via
`runtime/cmake/dn2cpp_embed_bytes.cmake`) and
`runtime/core/intrinsics/dn2cpp_http2_stream.cpp` hands that array to curl as
`CURLOPT_CAINFO_BLOB`.

A **vendored** bundle rather than the host's trust store because Mbed TLS has no
platform-trust-store integration at all — curl's `lib/vtls/mbedtls.c` implements
no `native_ca_store` arm, unlike the Schannel/Secure Transport/OpenSSL backends —
so with an mbedTLS backend and no bundle, *every* TLS handshake fails to verify.
Shipping the bytes in the binary is also the only shape that is the same on every
platform dn2cpp targets: an Android APK, an iOS bundle and a wasm module each
carry their payload differently, and none of them has a `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` for
`fopen` to reach.

## Version

- **`cacert.pem`, dated 2026-07-16** (its own header: `Certificate data from
  Mozilla as of: Thu Jul 16 03:12:01 2026 GMT`), 186,446 bytes, **119**
  certificates.
- Downloaded **2026-07-27** from `https://curl.se/ca/cacert.pem` — the
  always-latest URL published at https://curl.se/docs/caextract.html.
- **sha256 of the vendored file:**
  `3ff344e30b9b1ed2971044eabb438a08f2e2245ddb5f8ab1a3ad8b63ab4eaf91`
  (measured on the downloaded artifact; the file vendored here is byte-identical
  to it).

Note the `SHA256:` line **inside** `cacert.pem`'s own header
(`e57912808daef7b2b0fa4df2ccf17e47aeaf26c839a38f85c76003ebafd866bd`) is *not* a
checksum of this file: it is the checksum of the Mozilla `certdata.txt` the
bundle was converted from. The hash above is the one to compare a re-download
against, and it changes on every upstream refresh.

**Why curl's copy rather than Mozilla's `certdata.txt` directly.** `certdata.txt`
is an NSS source file in a bespoke format, not PEM; converting it is what curl's
`mk-ca-bundle.pl` does (this file's header records `version 1.33`), and the
conversion is where the trust-bit filtering lives — only roots Mozilla marks as
trusted for *server authentication* are emitted. Vendoring the converted artifact
keeps that filtering upstream, where it is maintained, and keeps a Perl script out
of this build.

## How it is built

Nothing here is compiled. `runtime/CMakeLists.txt`'s `DN2CPP_USE_CURL` arm runs

```sh
cmake -DIN=third_party/cacert/cacert.pem \
      -DOUT=<build>/generated/dn2cpp_ca_bundle.cpp \
      -DSYM=dn2cpp_ca_bundle_pem \
      -P runtime/cmake/dn2cpp_embed_bytes.cmake
```

as a build step, and adds the generated `.cpp` to `dn2cpp_runtime`'s sources. It
defines

```c
extern const unsigned char dn2cpp_ca_bundle_pem[];   // the file's bytes, verbatim
extern const unsigned int  dn2cpp_ca_bundle_pem_len; // 186446
```

which `dn2cpp_http2_stream.cpp` declares and passes to `CURLOPT_CAINFO_BLOB` on every
request. **The generated file is a build artifact and is never committed** — it
lives under the build tree, is ~1 MB of hex, and would otherwise have to be
regenerated by hand every time this bundle is refreshed.

`CURLOPT_CAINFO_BLOB` rather than `CURLOPT_CAINFO`: the blob form takes the bytes
in memory, so the same line of code works on a desktop, inside an APK and inside a
wasm module. A file path would work on exactly one of the three.

The bundle is **not** the only trust anchor source at run time: setting
`DN2CPP_HTTP_CAINFO=<path>` in the environment makes the transport pass that file
as `CURLOPT_CAINFO` *instead* of the embedded blob (see the design-contract
comment in `dn2cpp_http2_stream.cpp`). That is for a corporate MITM proxy's root, or
for a gate that needs a self-signed certificate trusted; it does not disable
verification, and there is no option that does.

## What was kept / dropped

Kept:

- **`cacert.pem`** — the published file, byte for byte, including its comment
  header. The header is what records the extraction date, the `mk-ca-bundle.pl`
  version and the `certdata.txt` checksum, so stripping it would throw away this
  vendor's provenance to save 1 KB.

Dropped:

- **`cacert.pem.sha256`**, and the detached signature files curl also publishes
  (`cacert.pem.asc`) — a checksum recorded next to the artifact it checksums
  proves nothing once both are in the same commit. The hash is written into this
  file instead, where a reviewer reads it before trusting a refresh.
- Every other bundle flavour on https://curl.se/docs/caextract.html (the
  `nss/` variants, the dated archives). One current bundle is the whole surface.

## Modifications to vendored source

**None.** `cacert.pem` is byte-identical to the download; the sha256 above is the
check.

Do not edit it to add a certificate. A private root belongs at run time, through
`DN2CPP_HTTP_CAINFO` — editing this file makes the next refresh (a plain
re-download, see below) silently drop the addition.

## License

**Mozilla Public License 2.0**, inherited from the Mozilla `certdata.txt` this
bundle is a mechanical conversion of (the source file carries the MPL-2.0 notice;
https://curl.se/docs/caextract.html states the same for the converted bundle).
`cacert.pem` itself carries **no license text in its header** — only provenance —
so there is no verbatim notice to copy out here; this section is the record.

MPL-2.0 is a per-*file* copyleft: it obliges anyone distributing this file, or a
modified form of it, to make that form available under MPL-2.0. This vendor makes
no modifications (see above), so that obligation is discharged by this directory
itself. It places no condition on the rest of a binary that merely embeds the
bytes (MPL-2.0 §3.3, "Larger Work"), which is the only thing dn2cpp does with it —
this is the one non-permissive license in `third_party/`, and that §3.3 boundary
is why it is acceptable here.

## Updating to a new version

**This vendor goes stale on a clock, unlike every other one here.** Certificates
expire, roots get revoked or distrusted, and new roots are added; a bundle that is
merely old does not fail loudly — it fails as a handshake error against one
particular host, months later, with nothing pointing at this directory. Mozilla
refreshes the store several times a year and curl republishes within days. Treat a
bundle older than ~6 months as due, and refresh it whenever an HTTPS gate starts
failing certificate verification against a host that works in a browser.

1. Re-download: `curl -fsSLo third_party/cacert/cacert.pem https://curl.se/ca/cacert.pem`.
2. Record the new sha256 (`shasum -a 256`), the new `Certificate data from
   Mozilla as of:` date out of the file's own header, the new byte count and the
   new certificate count (`grep -c 'BEGIN CERTIFICATE'`) in the "Version" section
   above. All four move together; a refresh that changes none of them was a no-op.
3. Nothing else changes — no build edit, no regeneration by hand. The embed step
   `DEPENDS` on this file, so the next build picks it up.
4. Re-run the HTTPS gate. A refresh that breaks verification against a public host
   is a bad download, not a bad bundle: check the sha256 first.

### Who refreshes, and when

The cadence is **gate-warning-driven, not calendar-driven**, and the tree itself
is what notices:

- `gates/build-and-run-http-get.sh` reads this bundle's own `Certificate data
  from Mozilla as of:` header on **every** run — warm cached-green runs
  included, since the check is keyed on the clock rather than on any input the
  gate cache hashes — and prints a `GATE-WARNING:` once the extraction date is
  ~6 months past (a louder one past a year); the runner tags the gate's pass
  line and lists every warning in the suite summary (`cacert_staleness_warn` /
  `gate_warn` in `gates/_common.sh`). A warning never fails the suite, at any
  age: the tree must not turn red on a calendar tick with no code change. A
  **missing or unparseable header** is a hard failure, by contrast — that is a
  property of the committed file, not of the clock.
- **The owner is whoever is running the suite when the warning fires.** Do the
  refresh (steps 1–4 above, minutes of work) in that change or a sibling commit.
  Nothing outside the suite watches this directory's date.
- `DN2CPP_HTTP_CAINFO` is a consumer's run-time escape hatch (see "How it is
  built"), not a refresh substitute: it rescues the one deployment that sets it,
  while every other binary built from a stale tree keeps the stale anchors.
